1 دَاحَتِ الشَّجَرَةُ , (K,) aor. تَدُوحُ; (TA;) and ↓ اداحت ; (A, TA;) The tree became great. (A, K.) ―
-b2- داح بَطْنُهُ, (K,) and ↓انداح, (A, K,) and ↓دوّح, (TA,) or ↓تدوّح, (so in a copy of the A,) His belly became swollen, or inflated, (A,) or big, (K,) and hung down, (A, K,) by reason of fatness or disease: (A, TA:) and so دَحَا and اندحى. (TA.) And داحت سُرَرُهُمْ [Their navels became swollen, and hung down]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
